The Applicant, **NEFA Power Trading Private Limited** , has filed the present Petition for the up-gradation of its inter-State trading licence in electricity from Category ‘V’ to Category ‘IV’.

Private Limited was granted a Category ‘V’ trading licence to trade in electricity as an

electricity trader in the whole of India, in accordance with the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of trading licence and other related matters), Regulations, 2020 (hereinafter referred to as ‘the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020’).

3. The Applicant has submitted that in view of the improved market conditions, growth expected in the power market, and looking at future business potential in power trading, NEFA Power Trading Private Limited seeks an up-gradation of its existing trading licence from Category ‘V’ to Category ‘IV’. The Applicant has submitted that it intends to engage in trading activities up to a quantum of 2,000 MUs in a financial year in terms of the provisions of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020.  The Applicant has further stated that its trading volumes have shown a consistent increase over the last financial year, which warrants an upgrade of the category of the licence. The Applicant has further stated that it will make the payment of the applicable licence fee or differential fee for Category IV trading licence in terms of the provisions of Regulation 15 (1) of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020 and will comply with the directions passed by the Commission.

4. The matter was called out for the hearing on 3.9.2026.  Learned counsel for the Applicant reiterated the submissions made in the instant Petition and further submitted that the Applicant fulfils all the requirements of Category IV inter-State Trading Licence as stipulated in the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020, amended from time to time.

5. We have considered the submissions of the Applicant. Regulation 9(4) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for Grant of Trading License and other Related Matters) Regulations, 2020 (the Trading Licence Regulations 2020) provides as under:

_“(4) The Trading Licensee shall make an appropriate application accompanied by prescribed fees for up-gradation of its licence to a higher category or downgradation of its licence to a lower category in order to fulfil the conditions of these regulations in accordance with the procedure specified in Regulation 15 of these regulations.”_

_(a) The Trading Licensee may at any time during a particular year apply for a higher category licence on the basis of the volume proposed to be traded in a particular Year._

_(b) The Trading Licensee shall file an application before the Commission for upgradation of its licence to a higher category as soon as he expects the trading volume to exceed the trading volume limit specified for the Trading Licensee’s existing category._

_(c) The Trading Licensee shall be granted an opportunity of being heard by the Commission before taking a decision on the application_

_(d) The Trading Licensee shall be required to submit the audited special balance sheet to support the compliance of Net Worth requirement for higher category licence._

7. The Applicant has filed the instant Petition for the upgradation of its inter-State trading licence in accordance with the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020. On perusal of the Petition, the Applicant, being an existing trading licensee, fulfils all technical requirements for the grant of a Category ‘IV’ inter-State trading licence. As regards the net worth requirements for Category ‘IV”, Regulation 3 (3) of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020 provides that a person applying for a Category ‘IV’ trading licence should have a net worth of Rs. 10 crore and should have maintained a minimum current ratio and liquidity ratio of 1:1 on the date of the Audited Special Balance Sheet accompanying the Petition.

Accordingly, we approve the upgradation of the inter-State trading licence of the Applicant from Category ‘V’ to Category ‘IV’ with effect from the date of issuance of the order. 7. In view of the above, it has been submitted by the Petitioner that it fulfils the requirements specified in Clause (1) of Regulation 3 of the Trading Licence Regulations.

13. On consideration of the above facts, after a preliminary examination, we find that the Petitioner meets the requirements as specified in the Trading Licence Regulations for the grant of a Category 'II' trading licence.  Accordingly, the Commission proposes to grant the Petitioner a Category 'II' trading licence. 4. During the course of virtual hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed seeking review of the order dated 23.3.2025 passed by this Commission in Petition No. 346/GT/2023. The Commission admitted the petition and directed the Respondents to file a reply and the Petitioner to file a rejoinder, if any.

5. During the virtual hearing, the counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Respondents have not yet filed their replies. Accordingly, the Commission adjourned the hearing and granted the Respondents a last opportunity to file a reply and the Petitioner a last opportunity to file its rejoinder, if any.

7. In its additional submission, the Petitioner stated that, as on the date of filing of the Review Petition, the contractual settlement with the EPC Contractor, M/s Braithwaite & Co. Ltd., was not finalised and, therefore, the actual amount recoverable towards LD was not placed before the Commission. The Petitioner further submitted that an amount of Rs. 3,05,34,136/- was later deducted and withheld as LD from M/S Braithwaite & Co. Ltd. in relation to the release of Retention Money against Erection & Commissioning of the Project. The said amount was less than the amount of Rs. 3,47,40,000/- deducted by the Commission from the Capital Cost of the Project in the Order dated 23.03.2025, and the same was requested to be taken on record and considered in the Review Petition.

8. During the virtual hearing, no one appeared on behalf of the Respondents, despite notice. After hearing learned counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission permitted the parties to file their written note of submissions on or before 31.7.2026. Subject to the above, the Commission reserved the matter for orders.

9. In compliance with the Record of Proceedings of the hearing dated 22.07.2026, the Petitioner submitted its written submission on 30.07.2026 and reiterated the contentions made in the petition as well as in the additional submission seeking review of the Order dated 23.03.2025.

10. The Commission has heard the learned counsel for the Petitioner and has carefully perused the Review Petition, the written submission and additional submission dated 21.07.2026, as well as the records of Petition No. 346/GT/2023 and the Order dated 23.03.2025 passed therein. The Commission also notes that no one appeared on behalf of the Respondents during the hearing, nor did they make any written submissions.

_(1) The Commission shall exercise jurisdiction to review its own orders, decisions, and directions in accordance with Clause (f) of sub-section (1) of Section 94 of the Act read with Section 114 and Order 47 of the Civil Procedure Code. (2) Any person aggrieved by a direction, decision, or order of the Commission, from which no appeal has been preferred, may file a review petition on the following grounds within forty days of the making of such decision, direction, or order: (a) Upon the discovery of new and important matter or evidence that, after the exercise of due diligence, was not within his knowledge or could not be produced by him at the time when the direction, decision, or order was passed or; (b) On account of some mistake or error apparent from the face of the record, or; (c) If there is any other sufficient reason to review the matter.”_

13. In the present case, the Petitioner has essentially sought reconsideration of four components of the capital cost/tariff, namely, (i) Project Management Cost, (ii) IDC, (iii) deduction towards Liquidated Damages, and (iv) Interest on Working Capital. The Commission has examined each of these claims only within the permissible grounds of review in the subsequent paragraphs.

20. **Commission’s Decision:** The Commission has dealt with this issue in detail, along with the reasons in paragraphs 58 and 59 of the Impugned Order. The Commission further observes that the 5% deduction in the Impugned Order was essentially linked to the Commission's finding that consumers should not bear the cost consequences of projectexecution inefficiency. The Commission's approach was a conscious and reasoned decision. The Commission has also considered the Petitioner’s additional submission dated 21.07.2026 regarding the amount of Rs. 305.34 Lakh stated to have been deducted and withheld as LD from the invoice of M/s Braithwaite & Co. Ltd. However, the Petitioner has not furnished the relevant invoice or supporting documents substantiating such deduction and withholding. Accordingly, the Commission finds no basis to modify its decision and rejects the Petitioner’s plea.

23. From the foregoing discussion, it is evident that each of the four issues raised by the Petitioner was either specifically considered in the Impugned Order or is sought to be raised on the basis of material which does not satisfy the requirements for review. In our considered view, the Petitioner has sought to re-argue the case on its merits, which is not permissible in review. The Review Petition has a limited purpose and cannot be an appeal in disguise. The Hon'ble Supreme Court has also enunciated the principles of review in its judgment in Kamlesh Verma v. Mayawati and Ors. [AIR 2006 SC 75]. We, therefore, find no reason to allow the Review Petition on this count. Accordingly, we hold that the Petitioner's prayer for review of the impugned order on these counts is not maintainable.
